title: Taiwanese American Society at Yale
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Society at Yale (TAS) is an undergraduate student organization at Yale University dedicated to promoting awareness of the cultural, political, and social aspects of Taiwanese American culture and fostering the broader Asian American community on campus. Founded in 1991 as the Taiwanese Club, the organization was later renamed the Yale College Taiwanese American Society to reflect the Taiwanese American identity of its membership. TAS is a member of Yale’s Pan-Asian Council and is listed among the internal organizations of the Asian Network at Yale.

TAS describes itself as non-exclusive and open to all students with an interest in Taiwan or Taiwanese American culture. Its recurring programs include cultural food events such as Dumpling Night and Tastes of Taiwan, a Big Sib program connecting students with local adopted heritage children through CASPY, speaker events, and a TAS Families mentorship program. The organization also distributes a weekly newsletter to its membership.

TAS has maintained a connection to the broader Taiwanese American student movement through its affiliation with the Intercollegiate Taiwanese American Students Association (ITASA). Yale hosted the second ITASA East Coast Conference in 1993, reflecting the organization’s early role in building the national Taiwanese American collegiate network.
